yard: A yard is the area around a house.
The children went out to play in the yard.
A yard is an imperial measure of length. One yard is three feet or 91.44 centimeters.
A soccer field is 110 yards long.
yay: You can say "yay!" when you are very happy or excited. People usually say this loudly, to show great emotion.
yawn: When someone yawns, they open their mouth wide and sometimes stretch their arms.
I can see that you're tired, because you keep yawning.
A yawn is the action of yawning.
He did three big yawns, then stood up to go upstairs to bed.
yam: A yam is a sweet potato.
A yam is a tropical climbing plant with roots that people eat.
Fry the potato or yam pieces until they are crisp and light brown.
yangon: Yangon is the largest city and previously the capital of Myanmar (Burma). It used to be called Rangoon.
ya: Will ya do this for me?
yacht: A yacht is a large boat used mostly for pleasure or racing.
The Queen had a yacht called "Britannia".
yarn: Yarn is a spun thread that is used for knitting, , or sewing.
A yarn is a story or tale that is incredible.
If someone is yarning, they are telling a story.
yank: A yank is a sudden, vigorous pull.
If you yank something, you pull it with a strong action.
yak: A yak is a type of cattle.
yap: If a tiny dog yaps, then it makes short loud sounds, but in an excited way.
The very tiny and cute dog yapped.
If you say that somebody yaps, you mean that they talk a lot in an obnoxious way.
Matthew loves to yap, and will always do so.
yawp: A yawp is a harsh cry or bark.
If a person yawps, they shout or exclaim hoarsely.
yankee: A Yankee is a person from the United States.
The Yankee visited his hometown in New England.
A Yankee is a person from the northern United States, especially in historical contexts.
During the Civil War, the Yankees fought against the Confederates.
If something is Yankee, it is related to the United States or its people.
He admired the Yankee style of baseball.
yayo: Yayo is another name for cocaine.
